mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for at least 3 consecutive months, lower real interest rates encourage equity investment, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the 30-day moving average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by rising consumer confidence (HOUST) simultaneously reduces labor market frictions and boosts demand, producing positive S&P 500 returns within 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month and HOUST rises by >5% in the same month
failure_condition: In 20-day window, returns are negative despite the trigger being met (Rank IC < -0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its moving average for two consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 5-day horizon, returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, it suggests a shift toward higher growth expectations, which predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite the inflation trigger (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 5% for a month indicates tightening labor market conditions and typically precedes a rate hike, which is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day horizon returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising industrial production (RSAFS) and employment (PAYEMS) together signal a supply-demand balance improving, which drives positive S&P 500 returns within 5 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by >2% and PAYEMS increases by >5% in the same month

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly change in the GDP deflator (implied by GDPC1) shows a steeper upward slope than the previous quarter, it suggests accelerating inflation expectations, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: First difference of GDPC1 (quarter-over-quarter) is positive and greater than previous quarter's first difference

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in consumer demand measured by HOUST for three consecutive months suggests a soft landing is unlikely, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases for three consecutive months
